Shikali Temple: Morning · Visit Shikali Temple outside Khokana, then continue to Rudrayani Temple in the village
Midday · Stop for lunch before heading to Bungamati
Afternoon · Visit Karya Binayak and Rato Machhindranath Temple
Dakshinkali Temple: Morning · Visit Dakshinkali Temple and allow time for darshan
Midday · Stop for lunch in Pharping
Afternoon · Explore Pharping or head back
Four Binayak Ganesh Temples: Morning · Start at Ashok Binayak in Maru, then visit Chandra Binayak in Chabahil
Midday · Visit Surya Binayak in Bhaktapur and stop for lunch
Afternoon · Continue to Jal Binayak in Chobhar
Kulekhani: Morning · Head to the reservoir at Markhu
Midday · Stop for lunch by the lake
Afternoon · Explore the lakeside before heading home
Bheda Farm: Morning · Start from Chitlang or Markhu
Midday · Explore the farm area on foot
Afternoon · Combine the outing with a stop at Kulekhani
Chandragiri Hills: Midday · Spend time at the viewpoint and stop for lunch
Afternoon · Leave time for the return journey
Godawari Botanical Garden: Morning · Explore the garden on foot
Bhaktapur Durbar Square: Afternoon · Continue exploring the old town
Nagarkot: Morning · Start with a viewpoint visit
Midday · Choose a restaurant for lunch
Afternoon · Take a short walk, then return
Panauti: Morning · Explore the old town on foot
Midday · Visit Indreshwor Temple and stop for lunch
Afternoon · Allow time for a riverside walk
Sankhu & Bajrayogini: Morning · Walk through the historic town
Afternoon · Return to town for a meal before heading back
Chitlang: Morning · Explore the village on foot
Afternoon · Leave time for the return drive
Namo Buddha: Afternoon · Pair the visit with Panauti if time allows

Bheda Farm.summary: The open slopes near Chitlang and Markhu make this a short countryside stop, with pasture views and room to slow down between destinations. Pair it with a longer walk in Chitlang or lunch by Kulekhani Reservoir.
stops: Take in the open pasture views before continuing toward Markhu.
Pause in Markhu for a walk by the reservoir or a meal by the water.
Bheda Farm.transport: Confirm the last stretch of the approach with your driver before leaving Chitlang or Markhu.
sources: Chitlang Organic Village Resort farm guide

Mahalaxmi Temple, Telkot.summary: Shree Pancha Mahalaxmi is a hillside temple near Telkot on the Bhaktapur side of the Nagarkot hills. It works as a short worship stop on a day that also includes Telkot or a viewpoint farther up the ridge.
stops: Shree Pancha Mahalaxmi Temple, Telkot, Bhaktapur
Visit the hillside shrine before heading farther up the Nagarkot ridge.
Make a short stop in Telkot between the temple and the ridge viewpoints.
Mahalaxmi Temple, Telkot.transport: Use the Pancha Mahalaxmi pin near Telkot and check the final turn before you leave the main road.

Kakani.summary: Kakani makes an easygoing hill outing beyond Kathmandu, with space for a short walk and views across the surrounding hills when skies are clear. Start at the viewpoint and leave time for the memorial park or lunch before the return drive.
stops: Look across the surrounding hills when the sky is clear.
Take a short walk around the memorial grounds after the viewpoint.
Kakani.bus: Ask for a passenger vehicle from Kathmandu toward Kakani. Confirm the boarding point, the closest drop-off to the viewpoint, and your return ride.
Kakani.transport: Set your navigation to Kakani Viewpoint. Use a separate pin for the memorial park if you are visiting both.

Banepa.summary: Banepa pairs a busy Kavre bazaar with quieter temple stops outside the centre. Walk through the market for a feel for the town, then make a separate stop at Chandeshwori Temple to the north.
history: Medieval palm-leaf records cited by Banepa Municipality refer to the settlement by earlier names, including Vinayapuri. The municipality also traces the town’s commercial roots to its long trading relationship with Tibet.
stops: Walk through the market streets before heading north to the temple.
Pause in the courtyard to look at the tiered shrine and its carved details.
Banepa.transport: Start near the town centre and use a separate pin for Chandeshwori Temple.

Budhanilkantha.summary: The centrepiece of Budhanilkantha is a stone image of Vishnu reclining on a serpent in a temple pool. The courtyard is an active place of worship, so allow time for darshan and give devotees space around the shrine.
stops: See the stone Vishnu reclining on a serpent in the temple pool.

White Gumba.summary: White Gumba is the Druk Amitabha Mountain Buddhist campus in Nagarjun, home to a community of Drukpa nuns. The uphill visit is best planned around public access to the grounds, with time to take in the hillside setting.
stops: Explore the hillside grounds when open to visitors and follow the monastery’s guidance.
White Gumba.transport: Confirm public access before taking the uphill approach to the monastery.

Kirtipur.summary: Kirtipur is a hilltop Newar town best explored on foot, from Bagh Bhairab Temple through the lanes toward Uma Maheshwar Temple. Leave time for a Newari meal and look out for views of the valley between the buildings.
history: Kirtipur was a fortified hill town in the Kathmandu Valley. It resisted Gorkha’s attempts to capture it before becoming part of Prithvi Narayan Shah’s expanding kingdom.
stops: Look for the three-tiered Newar shrine dedicated to Bhairab in tiger form.
Continue through the old lanes to the hilltop shrine for a view over the valley.
Kirtipur.transport: Plan to explore the old town on foot and arrange a pickup point outside the narrow lanes.

Dhulikhel.summary: Dhulikhel offers two different ways to spend the day: a walk through the old town or a climb toward Kalidevi Temple. Start in the lanes and squares if you prefer a gentler outing, or build the day around the 1,000 Steps and the hilltop views.
stops: Wander through the lanes and squares for a gentler outing before the hill climb.
Follow the stone steps uphill toward Kalidevi Temple, taking breaks as needed.
Dhulikhel.bus: Ask for a Dhulikhel-bound bus and confirm the boarding point and last return. Get off near the town centre for the old-town walk.
Dhulikhel.transport: Choose the old town or the lower end of the 1,000 Steps as your drop-off, depending on where you want to start.

Kathmandu Durbar Square.summary: Walk through Basantapur to see the Hanuman Dhoka palace precinct, tiered temples and carved windows around Kumari Ghar. The courtyards and squares sit in the middle of a working city, so the visit can extend into the surrounding lanes.
history: Hanuman Dhoka was a royal palace precinct. The palace, temples and public squares show how court life and worship shared the centre of historic Kathmandu. The precinct is one of seven monument zones in the Kathmandu Valley World Heritage site.
stops: Explore the former royal palace precinct and its courtyards off Durbar Square.
Look up at the carved wooden windows of the Kumari’s residence from the square.

Patan Durbar Square.summary: Patan’s royal square brings stone temples and brick palace courtyards together in the centre of Lalitpur. Spend time at Krishna Mandir and the Patan Museum to see Newar craftsmanship at street level and up close.
history: Patan’s Durbar Square grew around its royal palace and the temples and public spaces beside it. The ensemble preserves examples of the valley’s Newar architecture and craftsmanship and is part of the Kathmandu Valley World Heritage site.
stops: Step inside the former palace to see religious art and examples of Newar craftsmanship.
Pause in the square to look at the stone temple and its carved tiers.

Bhaktapur Durbar Square.summary: Start among the palace buildings and carved façades of Durbar Square, then walk to Nyatapola in Taumadhi and on to Pottery Square. The route combines royal architecture with the everyday work and street life of old Bhaktapur.
history: Bhaktapur’s royal square was a centre of court and religious life. The palace, temples and squares preserve evidence of the city’s historic role and are included in the Kathmandu Valley World Heritage site.
stops: Look up at the carved wooden windows along the palace façade, then see the Golden Gate beside it.
Take in the five-tiered temple from Taumadhi Square and look for the guardian figures lining its staircase.
Look for potters shaping clay on traditional wheels and earthenware set out to dry.
sources: Bhaktapur Municipality guide to the squares

Pharping.summary: Pharping brings together Buddhist and Hindu pilgrimage sites on the southern side of the valley. Visit Asura Cave and Vajrayogini Temple as separate stops around town, then continue to Dakshinkali if you have time.
stops: Make time for the Vajrayogini shrine before continuing to the cave.
Visit the Buddhist pilgrimage cave and give worshippers space in the small shrine area.
Allow time for darshan at the shrine dedicated to Kali.

Swayambhunath.summary: Swayambhunath crowns a hill above Kathmandu with a white stupa, prayer wheels and smaller shrines around its base. Follow the circuit at your own pace and pause where the hill opens onto views across the city.
history: UNESCO identifies the Swayambhu stupa as the Kathmandu Valley’s oldest Buddhist monument. The stupa and the religious buildings around it make up one of the valley’s seven World Heritage monument zones.
stops: Walk around the hilltop stupa past prayer wheels and smaller shrines.
See preserved specimens of Nepal’s wildlife at the museum below the stupa.
Swayambhunath.transport: Check which entrance suits your group. The main stairway involves a steep climb.

Kathmandu Fun Park.summary: A compact amusement park in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu Fun Park is a central stop for families looking for a few rides and a snack break. Its location makes it easy to combine with a short walk around Ratna Park or a longer outing to Basantapur.

Natural History Museum.summary: Tribhuvan University’s museum below Swayambhu offers a close look at Nepal’s wildlife through preserved animals and insect specimens. It suits a short indoor outing and pairs naturally with a visit to the stupa above.
history: Tribhuvan University established the museum in 1975 at the foot of Swayambhu hill. Its collections document Nepal’s biodiversity for research and education.
stops: Look for Nepal’s preserved animal and insect specimens in the museum galleries.
Natural History Museum.bus: The museum recommends getting off at Swayambhu Ring Road and continuing on foot to the museum complex.
Natural History Museum.transport: Use the museum’s own pin for drop-off. It is below the stupa, so the Swayambhunath hilltop entrance is a separate stop.
Natural History Museum.visitNote: Check the museum’s seasonal hours and Saturday closures. Bring student identification if you plan to ask for the student rate.

Jump KTM, Jhamsikhel.summary: This indoor trampoline park in Jhamsikhel is a destination for active play in Lalitpur. Give children time to get comfortable on the equipment and check with the branch about age limits and suitable sessions.
stops: Jump Jhamsikhel Indoor Trampoline Park, Lalitpur
Plan an indoor jumping session and ask the branch which session suits younger children.
Jump KTM, Jhamsikhel.visitNote: Ask the Jhamsikhel branch about booking a session, grip socks, and rules for younger children.

Whoopee Land.summary: Whoopee Land in Chobhar combines waterslides with amusement rides. Families can plan the outing around the water park or choose a shorter visit for the rides, depending on what is operating and what suits the group.
stops: Whoopee Land Amusement and Water Park, Chobhar
Choose between the waterslides and amusement rides based on what is open.
Whoopee Land.visitNote: Confirm that the water rides are running before you pack swimwear. Check each attraction’s height restrictions at the park.

Kathmandu Fun Valley.summary: Kathmandu Fun Valley is a water park in Palanse near Sanga, built around pools and slides. It makes a different sort of family outing from the nearby temple and heritage visits, especially when the wave pool and water attractions are running.
stops: Spend time at the wave pool and slides when those attractions are operating.
Kathmandu Fun Valley.visitNote: Check the latest pool and slide availability before travelling and ask about children’s access to individual attractions.

Chandragiri Hills.summary: The cable car climbs from the valley to a ridge with mountain views on clear days. Spend time around Bhaleshwor Mahadev Temple, then choose between a viewpoint break and the playground if you are visiting with children.
history: The ridge formed part of an old route into the Kathmandu Valley. Local tradition associates it with Prithvi Narayan Shah’s view of Kathmandu during the period of Gorkha expansion. Bhaleshwor Mahadev remains a pilgrimage stop on the ridge.
stops: Ride up to the ridge for the viewpoint, Bhaleshwor Mahadev Temple or the playground.
Chandragiri Hills.visitNote: Check the cable car’s operating hours and ask about the last ride down before spending time at the playground.

Bagh Bhairab Temple.summary: Bagh Bhairab Temple is a tiered shrine in old Kirtipur dedicated to Bhairab in tiger form. Make it the first stop on a walk through the old town and continue toward Uma Maheshwar Temple if you want a longer hilltop route.
history: Kirtipur Municipality traces the temple’s construction to the reign of King Shivadev, from 1099 to 1126, citing the Gopal dynasty chronicle. The town honours Bagh Bhairab as its protector and holds an annual jatra in his name.
stops: Look for the three-tiered Newar shrine dedicated to Bhairab in tiger form.
Bagh Bhairab Temple.bus: Ask for a bus to Kirtipur and confirm where to get off for the old town. Continue on foot to Bagh Bhairab Temple and check your return service before setting out.
Bagh Bhairab Temple.transport: Use the temple pin to plan a drop-off near old Kirtipur. Allow time to walk through the narrow lanes from where the vehicle can stop.

Indrayani Temple (Luti Ajima).summary: Luti Ajima is a riverside Indrayani shrine near the Bishnumati. Combine time at the shrine with a short neighbourhood walk toward Shobha Bhagwati or nearby Bijeshwari.
stops: Pause at the Indrayani shrine by the Bishnumati before walking toward Shobha Bhagwati.
sources: Tribhuvan University study of Kathmandu’s Ajima shrines

Mhepi Ajima Temple.summary: A wooded hill separates this Ajima shrine from the busy streets of Mhepi below. The hillside setting makes it a compact worship stop with a short walk as part of the visit.
stops: Follow the short uphill approach to the wooded shrine above the neighbourhood.
sources: Tribhuvan University study of Kathmandu’s Ajima shrines

Bijeshwari Temple.summary: Bijeshwari is a Vajrayogini shrine near Shobha Bhagwati in Kathmandu. Its location close to the Bishnumati makes it easy to pair with Luti Ajima on a short pilgrimage walk.
stops: Visit the Vajrayogini shrine near Shobha Bhagwati and pair it with nearby Luti Ajima.
sources: Wikimedia Commons temple photo and location

Santaneshwor Mahadev Temple.summary: Santaneshwor Mahadev is a Shiva shrine in Jharuwarasi, Lalitpur. Set aside time for worship and the approach to the temple, then continue toward Godawari if you want a second stop in the area.
stops: Allow time for worship at this Shiva shrine before continuing toward Godawari.

Chonga Ganesh Temple.summary: The Chonga Ganesh shrine sits beside the Sallaghari pine grove in Bhaktapur. Start with darshan, then use a permitted spot in the grove if your group is staying for a picnic.
stops: Start with darshan, then walk in the pine grove beside the temple.
Chonga Ganesh Temple.picnic: The pine grove near the temple is used for picnics. Ask locally where groups can set up and whether cooking is allowed.

Surya Binayak Temple.summary: This wooded hillside shrine is one of the Ganesh temples in the Four Binayak pilgrimage circuit. Allow time for the uphill approach, and plan a separate picnic stop on the surrounding hillside if visiting with a group.
stops: Follow the uphill approach through the wooded grounds to the Ganesh shrine.
Surya Binayak Temple.picnic: Picnic areas are available on the surrounding hillside. Check reservation arrangements before bringing a group.

Tribhuvan Park.summary: Tribhuvan Park in Thankot is a public park with designated picnic grounds. It is suited to a group outing centred on a shared meal, with time to walk around the grounds before heading home.
stops: Take a walk around the grounds and settle in for a meal at a designated picnic spot.
Tribhuvan Park.picnic: Check the park’s current picnic booking options and fees before a group visit.

Balaju Baisdhara Park.summary: Balaju Baisdhara Park combines ponds, garden paths and historic stone water spouts. The park works for a short city walk or a longer picnic in a designated shelter.
stops: Follow the garden paths past ponds and the historic stone water spouts.
sources: Kathmandu Metropolitan City schedule of picnic shelters
Balaju Baisdhara Park.picnic: Kathmandu Metropolitan City lists designated picnic spaces here. Ask the park about reservations and current fees.

Manjushree Park.summary: Manjushree Park overlooks Chobhar Gorge, where the Bagmati passes through a narrow channel. The lawns and paths make the gorge an easy outing, and nearby Jal Binayak adds a temple stop if you have time.
history: Kirtipur Municipality records that the gorge area was quarried for limestone for more than two decades before it was developed into Manjushree Park.
stops: Walk the park paths for a view of where the Bagmati narrows through Chobhar Gorge.
Manjushree Park.picnic: A local family picnic spot. Check with park staff for garden rules and group arrangements.

Sangdaha Picnic Spot.summary: Sangdaha is a wooded picnic area in Changunarayan with shelters among the pines. Plan the outing around a picnic and a short walk in the forest, with Changu Narayan Temple as a separate stop.
stops: Look for the picnic shelters among the pines and take a short forest walk.
Sangdaha Picnic Spot.picnic: The municipal inventory lists several picnic areas in the forest. Confirm current access, facilities, and cooking rules before visiting.

1,000 Steps, Dhulikhel.summary: The stepped route climbs from Dhulikhel toward Kalidevi Temple. Make the staircase the main outing and take breaks on the way up, or combine part of the climb with an old-town walk.
stops: Follow the stone steps uphill toward Kalidevi Temple, taking breaks as needed.
Pause at the hilltop shrine after the climb up Dhulikhel’s 1,000 Steps.
sources: Dhulikhel Municipality’s Kalidevi and 1,000 Steps listing

Central Zoo.summary: Central Zoo in Jawalakhel brings together animal exhibits and spaces where children can take a break. Choose a manageable circuit through the grounds and leave time for the aquarium or children’s area.
history: Rana prime minister Juddha Shamsher established the zoo as a private collection in 1932. It passed into government ownership after the political changes of 1950 and opened to the public in 1956.
National Trust for Nature Conservation report
stops: Pick a short loop through the animal exhibits and leave time for the aquarium or children’s area.
Central Zoo.visitNote: Check the official visitor page for tickets and opening days. Plan a shorter loop or a break at the children’s area for younger visitors.
sources: National Trust for Nature Conservation visitor information

Simulation Science Center.summary: This science centre in Chobhar is geared toward learning through hands-on demonstrations. It is a good fit for a school or family outing if a visit can be arranged, with Chobhar Gorge nearby for a second stop.
stops: Ask which hands-on demonstrations are available and whether your visit needs to be arranged in advance.
Simulation Science Center.visitNote: Confirm whether the centre accepts walk-ins or requires advance arrangements for a group.

National Museum of Nepal.summary: The National Museum in Chhauni brings Nepal’s art and history together in several collections. Give yourself time to move between galleries, then pair the visit with Swayambhunath for a longer day in western Kathmandu.
history: The museum grew out of a weapons collection at Chhauni that was known as Chhauni Silkhana. The former arsenal building now houses the historical galleries. The complex later added galleries for art and Buddhist collections.
stops: Explore the historical, art and Buddhist collections in the museum buildings.
Follow the stupa circuit for a view over Kathmandu after the museum visit.
sources: Nepal Tourism Board’s National Museum guide

Adinath Lokeshwar Temple.summary: Adinath Lokeshwar Temple sits above Chobhar village. Its hilltop setting offers a different experience from the riverside shrine of Jal Binayak, which makes a natural second stop.
stops: Start with the hilltop shrine above Chobhar before heading down toward the river.
Visit the Ganesh shrine beside the Bagmati, close to Chobhar Gorge.

Bajra Barahi Temple.summary: A Barahi shrine stands in a wooded grove outside Chapagaon. The visit combines worship with a short walk among the trees, with Chapagaon nearby for a stop in town.
stops: Combine darshan at the Barahi shrine with a short walk in the surrounding grove.

Nil Barahi Temple.summary: Nil Barahi is a shrine in the wooded Tigani area near Bode. It is closely tied to the community’s masked dance tradition, and a visit can be paired with a walk through Bode itself.
history: The shrine is tied to Bode’s Nil Barahi masked dance. Performers take on the roles of deities during the community observance, keeping the shrine connected to festival life beyond daily worship.
stops: Nil Barahi Temple, Bode, Madhyapur Thimi
Visit the wooded Tigani shrine associated with Bode’s Nil Barahi masked dance.

Chandeshwori Temple.summary: This goddess temple lies north of Banepa’s centre and offers a quieter stop after the market. The temple and bazaar make a compact half-day outing with two distinct sides of the town.
stops: Pause in the courtyard to look at the tiered shrine and its carved details.

Matsya Narayan Temple.summary: The Vishnu shrine at Machhegaun is associated with Matsya, the deity’s fish incarnation. It is a local pilgrimage stop and the focus of the Purushottam Mela when the festival takes place.
stops: Visit the shrine dedicated to Matsya, the fish incarnation of Vishnu.
sources: The Rising Nepal report from Machhegaun

Doleshwor Mahadev Temple.summary: Doleshwor Mahadev is a Shiva pilgrimage site in Sipadol, Bhaktapur, associated with Kedarnath. Allow time for worship here, then continue to Ashapuri if you are planning a longer temple outing.
history: In 2009, the chief priest of Kedarnath formally recognised Doleshwor Mahadev as the head of Kedarnath in pilgrimage tradition. The association draws Shiva devotees to the temple in Sipadol.
stops: See the Nandi statue in the courtyard and allow time for worship at the Shiva shrine.
Continue to the gold-roofed Shiva temple for a second pilgrimage stop.

Ashapuri Mahadev Temple.summary: Ashapuri Mahadev is a Shiva temple in Suryabinayak with a gold-roofed shrine. It can be a short visit on its own or the second stop on a pilgrimage outing from Doleshwor Mahadev.
history: Suryabinayak Municipality records a local legend that a Shiva linga appeared from the ground after villagers prayed during a drought. The story explains the shrine’s association with the fulfilment of wishes.
stops: Look for the gold-roofed shrine and pause in the grounds after darshan.
Stop at the Shiva shrine associated with Kedarnath and look for Nandi in the courtyard.
Ashapuri Mahadev Temple.bus: Take a bus toward Suryabinayak Chowk. Ask about onward transport to Ashapuri before leaving the chowk, and confirm your return arrangements.
Ashapuri Mahadev Temple.transport: Use the Ashapuri temple pin in Suryabinayak Ward 8 for the drive. Check the final approach and drop-off locally.

Ichangu Narayan Temple.summary: Ichangu Narayan is a Vishnu shrine west of Swayambhu. It is one of the valley’s four Narayan shrines and makes a short temple stop on the Nagarjun side of Kathmandu.
stops: Spend time at one of the valley’s four Narayan shrines west of Swayambhu.

Shikali Temple.summary: Shikali Temple sits outside Khokana, away from the village’s central lanes. Start in the village at Rudrayani Temple or visit Shikali first, then walk into Khokana to see the setting of the community’s jatra.
stops: Walk out from the village to the shrine associated with Khokana’s Shikali Jatra.
Shikali Temple.picnic: Ask locally where picnics are permitted around Khokana. Picnic facilities near the temple are unconfirmed.
sources: Tribhuvan University study of Shikali Jatra

Rudrayani Temple.summary: Rudrayani Temple stands in central Khokana among the village’s lanes and courtyards. It gives a visit a clear starting point before exploring the settlement or continuing out to Shikali Temple.
history: The village’s temple sits within a traditional pattern of courtyards and lanes. Nepal’s heritage submission for Khokana documents the village’s mother-goddess shrine and mustard-oil production as part of its living heritage.
stops: Start at the village shrine before exploring Khokana’s central lanes and courtyards.
sources: UNESCO Tentative List entry for Khokana

Karya Binayak Temple.summary: Karya Binayak is a Ganesh shrine in Bungamati. Pair it with the Rato Machhindranath shrine to experience two different places of worship on one village visit.
stops: Stop at the Ganesh shrine before continuing to the Rato Machhindranath temple.

Rato Machhindranath Temple.summary: This Bungamati shrine is associated with Rato Machhindranath, or Bung Dhya, the central deity of Lalitpur’s chariot festival. Plan the shrine as part of a walk through Bungamati and include Karya Binayak if you have time.
history: Tradition identifies Bungamati as the birthplace of the deity also known as Bung Dhya. Lalitpur’s chariot procession honours Rato Machhindranath, who is associated with rain and the agricultural season.
stops: Visit the shrine of Bung Dhya, the deity honoured in Lalitpur’s chariot festival.

Jal Binayak Temple.summary: Jal Binayak is a Ganesh shrine beside the Bagmati at Chobhar. The riverside approach and nearby gorge make it a natural companion to Manjushree Park or the hilltop Adinath temple.
history: Known locally as Kwoyena, Jal Binayak is one of the valley’s celebrated Ganesh shrines. Kirtipur Municipality dates the temple to the 16th century and notes that families come here for worship and ceremonies.
stops: Visit the Ganesh shrine beside the Bagmati, close to Chobhar Gorge.

Dakshinkali Temple.summary: This shrine south of Pharping is dedicated to Kali. Give yourself time for darshan at the temple and continue to Pharping for another pilgrimage stop or a meal on the way back.
stops: Allow time for darshan at the shrine dedicated to Kali.
Explore the town’s shrines after visiting Dakshinkali, or stop for a meal on the way back.
Dakshinkali Temple.bus: Ask for a bus toward Dakshinkali via Pharping. Confirm whether the service goes to the temple area and where to catch the last return.
Dakshinkali Temple.transport: Follow the road via Pharping and set the destination to Dakshinkali Temple. Check the closest drop-off or parking on arrival.

Four Binayak Ganesh Temples.summary: This route links four Ganesh shrines across the Kathmandu Valley: Ashok Binayak in Maru, Chandra Binayak in Chabahil, Surya Binayak in Bhaktapur and Jal Binayak in Chobhar. Plan the circuit as several stops with travel time between them, or split it into two outings.
stops: Also known as Maru Ganesh. Pair this stop with Kathmandu Durbar Square if time allows.
Also known as Rakta Binayak. Use the Chabahil pin when planning your route.
Allow time for the uphill approach and check access if someone in your group has difficulty with stairs.
The shrine is by the Bagmati. Pair it with Kirtipur if you split the circuit over two days.
Four Binayak Ganesh Temples.transport: Allow time for cross-valley travel between temples. Confirm local worship times and follow each shrine’s photography guidance.
sources: Tribhuvan University CNAS journal on Valley shrine groupings

Nagarkot.summary: Nagarkot is a ridge getaway east of Kathmandu, best known for sunrise and long Himalayan views when the sky is clear. A short ridge walk and breakfast make an outing on their own, or you can add Changu Narayan on the return.
stops: Go early for sunrise and look for the Himalayan skyline on a clear morning.
Explore the hilltop Vishnu shrine and its stone sculpture on the return from Nagarkot.
Nagarkot.bus: Confirm the current boarding point and any connection for Nagarkot. If you are going for sunrise, check whether a passenger service runs early enough.
Nagarkot.transport: Set directions to the specific viewpoint or hotel you plan to visit. The village and view tower are separate stops.

Changu Narayan Temple.summary: The hilltop Vishnu temple sits inside the traditional settlement of Changu Narayan. Give yourself time for the stone sculpture and temple precinct, then make a separate stop at the forest picnic ground if that is part of your plan.
history: A fifth-century inscription at Changu Narayan is one of the earliest recorded inscriptions in the Kathmandu Valley. The temple precinct and traditional settlement together form one of the Kathmandu Valley World Heritage monument zones.
stops: Take time for the stone sculptures and early inscription in the temple precinct.
Look for the forest picnic ground near the bus park, separate from the temple.
Changu Narayan Temple.picnic: The municipality lists a picnic ground in the forest near the bus park, separate from the temple. Check access, fees, and group arrangements before visiting.

Godawari Botanical Garden.summary: Paths wind past ponds and themed plant collections at the foot of Phulchowki. Look for orchids, medicinal plants and the rock garden, then take a break at one of the designated shelters if you brought a picnic.
history: King Mahendra inaugurated the Royal Botanical Garden in 1962. It was renamed the National Botanical Garden in 2006 and continues to conserve living plant collections for research and public education.
Godawari Botanical Garden.picnic: The garden lists designated rest areas for dry picnics. Bring prepared food. The garden prohibits cooking on site.

Sankhu & Bajrayogini.summary: Start in Sankhu’s old Newar lanes, where public squares and small shrines break up the walk through town. Stone steps lead uphill to Bajrayogini, a pilgrimage site for Hindu and Buddhist devotees that can be paired with Salinadi.
history: Sankhu dates to the Lichchhavi period and stood on an old trade route to Tibet. Nepal’s Department of Archaeology dates the hill’s main Bajrayogini temple complex to the mid-17th century. Nepal submitted the town and temple together to UNESCO’s Tentative List in 2008.
Sankhu & Bajrayogini.picnic: Ask locally about permitted picnic areas around Sankhu. Picnic facilities near the temple are unconfirmed.

Panauti.summary: Walk through Panauti’s old town toward Indreshwor Mahadev Temple and the riverside ghats. The compact lanes and courtyard shrines reward an unhurried visit, with Namo Buddha as a separate stop outside town.
history: At the meeting of the Roshi and Punyamati rivers, the medieval complex grew around Indreshwor Mahadev Temple, traditionally dated to 1294. It also includes the 17th-century Brahmayani Temple and historic rest houses. Nepal submitted the complex to UNESCO’s Tentative List in 1996.
stops: See the timber carvings at the temple, then walk toward the riverside ghats.
Continue from Panauti to the pilgrimage stupa and monastery as a separate stop.

Namo Buddha.summary: At Namo Buddha, a pilgrimage stupa and the hilltop Thrangu Tashi Yangtse Monastery offer two places to spend time. Plan for the uphill approach between stops and leave room for a quiet walk around the monastery grounds.
stops: Thrangu Tashi Yangtse Monastery, Namo Buddha
Allow time for the uphill approach and a quiet walk around the monastery grounds.

Chitlang.summary: Chitlang is a village on the far side of Chandragiri, suited to a slow walk through the settlement before lunch. The outing can continue into the pasture country near Bheda Farm or down toward Kulekhani Reservoir.
history: Chitlang lies on a historic approach to the Kathmandu Valley through Chandragiri. The Nepal Tourism Board records a local account that members of the Malla royal family took refuge there after Prithvi Narayan Shah’s conquest in the 18th century.
stops: Slow down with a walk through the village before returning from the reservoir.
Continue from Chitlang toward Markhu for a change from village lanes to lakeside views.

Kulekhani.summary: At Kulekhani, the hills around Indra Sarowar frame a quiet lakeside stop. Start near Markhu for a walk or a meal by the water, then continue to Chitlang if you have time for a village visit.
history: The area lies at the southern end of the historic Kathmandu approach through Chandragiri and Chitlang. Today Indra Sarowar is the reservoir that feeds the Kulekhani hydropower system.
stops: Start near Markhu and pause by the water for a short walk or lunch.
Slow down with a walk through the village before returning from the reservoir.

Take a break inside the park or look for food around Pradarshani Marg.
Several food stalls in Basantapur if you’re heading toward Durbar Square.

Take a food break in Bhrikutimandap or head to Basantapur for lunch.
Add a short walk around Ratna Park or continue to Kathmandu Durbar Square.

blogPosts.title: A day trip to Nagarkot for sunrise
blogPosts.intro: Plan an early viewpoint stop, a slow breakfast, and an optional visit to Changu Narayan.
sections: Start with the view

Pick a viewpoint before departure and check the forecast the night before. An early start gives you time to settle in before sunrise. Bring a warm layer for the ridge and plan breakfast after the viewpoint.
Choose your second stop
Stay near Nagarkot for a short walk or continue to Changu Narayan. If you plan to walk the ridge route, arrange your return from the temple in advance.
Plan the return
Confirm your pickup point and last return if you’re using public transport. Allow time for breakfast and the return journey when deciding whether to add a second stop.
sources: Nepal Tourism Board’s Nagarkot sunrise guide

blogPosts.title: Chitlang, Markhu and Kulekhani in a day
blogPosts.intro: Pair a Chitlang village walk with lunch by the reservoir, and add Bheda Farm if time allows.
sections: Morning in Chitlang

Start with a village walk and decide how much walking you want to do before lunch. Nepal Tourism Board describes a walking route from Chitlang toward the reservoir and a longer motor road. Plan transport around the route you choose.
Lunch by the water
Use Markhu as your lakeside stop at Indra Sarowar. Leave time for lunch and a walk before starting the return leg. Confirm availability directly with a local operator if boating is part of your plan.
Fit in Bheda Farm
Treat the farm as an optional stop around Chitlang and Markhu. Check the approach locally and leave enough time for the return, especially if your group wants a longer village walk.
sources: Nepal Tourism Board’s Chitlang and Kulekhani route
Chitlang Organic Village Resort’s Bheda Farm guide

blogPosts.title: Three Kathmandu Valley outings with kids
blogPosts.intro: Choose a garden walk in Godawari, a heritage stop in Bhaktapur, or a village outing in Chitlang.
sections: Godawari for an outdoor morning
Choose a short walk through the botanical garden and set a turnaround point everyone can manage. Plan a snack break and check opening hours before setting off.
Bhaktapur for a heritage walk
Start at Durbar Square, look for carved windows and courtyards, then stop for lunch. A short route with room for pauses makes it easier to adapt the day to younger children.
Chitlang for a village day
Make the village the main stop and choose a lunch venue ahead of time. If the group has energy for another walk, decide on the day how much to add.
sources: Nepal Tourism Board’s guide to travel with children

blogPosts.title: A heritage walk and temple visit in Sankhu
blogPosts.intro: Walk through Sankhu before visiting Bajrayogini Temple on a single outing.
sections: Begin in the town
Give yourself time to explore Sankhu on foot before heading to the temple. Start with a short loop and leave room for lunch or tea after the shrine visit.
Continue to Bajrayogini
Bajrayogini is a pilgrimage site for Buddhist and Hindu devotees. Follow the directions from town, allow time for the uphill approach, and check access locally if your group needs an easier route.
Choose a return point
If you’re meeting a driver or using public transport, agree on a return point before leaving town. The destination guide includes a map and directions with Sankhu and Bajrayogini as separate stops.
